dayZeroMeeting: ^Nice you've already figured out how the phone works, off to a good start.
^I'm sure you have a lot of questions but there's one very important thing you need to know.
^My dear employee. I... am... your... father.

^Okay, okay. Maybe that was a bit dramatic... I've been immersing myself in human culture and there are these things called movies, I recently picked up this new one I think it was called "Space Wars"? so there's this gu-- sorry not important, anyway...
^Technically we Genie can't actually have children because there's simply no need.
^Instead, when a Genie decides it's time to pass their duties on they create a sort of hollow lifeform.
^Once this lifeform is created, it kicks off a transitional phase where the 'parental' being must impart all of their wisdom to their replacement.
^Given that we are immortal beings that live for centuries, this process goes against our nature which makes it extremely taxing.
^This comes with it's fair share of side effects of course, but the main one is a phenomenon that's akin to what humans call "ageing".
^Anyways we're getting off track and I don't want to waste too much of your time before you've actually started working for me.
^I'll quickly walk you through the process of how we do things here but before we start do you have any questions?
dayZeroQuestions: ^Why go through such an unnatural process?

c-0:
^I guess one of my ancestors decided it would be the best way to keep any one of us from holding that power for too long, to keep us in check.

^Given that we genie hold so much power and can each exist for centuries we have become beings of habit, or I guess more accurately: beings of tradition.

^It was most likely put in place by the first because I can't imagine anyone else down the track doing so. Like I said; it's not exactly in our nature to switch things up.

^My father believed it was about building up a sort of continuous stream of knowledge. Each of us holds the same information as our predecessors, sure...

^But he believed that when each predecessor faces eternal retirement, their consciousness gets added to that stream of knowledge. So that they get to live on as a collective subconscious, represented by its freshest and most refined.

^And that it's through this constant compounding that we have no choice but to evolve when the time is right.
c-1:
^To put it simply, I have created this company and the environment you find yourself in as part of a radical experiment to bring genie and humankind closer together.

^And you my dear employee, are a VERY key part of that.

^Basically since both of our kinds have existed, humans and genies have been intertwined in a kind of cosmic-symbiotic relationship.

^Humans are creatures that inherently desire more than they can give, at least in terms of any one human. Genies are beings that can give-- nay, create --virtually anything while having no inherent desire to take for ourselves.

^What do we get out of it? Simple. It's what we exist for. Simply put, we not only gain purpose from providing for others but also derive a kind of sustenance from it.

^I believe the way us genies conduct our purpose is greatly outdated any if we're going to be able to understand each other better we need to not only open ourselves up to learning from humans but also increasing our reach.

^Hence the switch from rubbing lamps to calling a free hotline.

^Plus I think humans really are fascinating, and why shouldn't we find ways to make our work fun?
c-2:
^No, just you. As I mentioned earlier it takes an incredbile amount of power to create another life.

^Well actually creating a husk much like yourself isn't the problem, the difficult part is the transfer of knowledge; the part that actually justifies such a taxing process.

^If I was to create more than one being to become my successor it would harm the transfer...

^Either by splitting the information between however many, or by effectively multiplying the time it would take which would likely result in the last of my lifeforce being drained before the transfer could complete.

^Ideally I'd love to have an entire call centre dedicated to this project but these things have to start somewhere.

^So consider yourself a pioneer of the wish-granting industry.

dayOneMeeting: ^Welcome to your first real day on the job!
^Well I say day but it's not like that really matters around here. I just make it a point to get as immersed in human culture as possible.
^It helps us understand them and their needs better.
^We're still getting things up and running in the advertising department so this should be a pretty chill day.
^Looks like you just have TWO callers today so I'll make it easy on you.
^Today's quota is ONE. All you have to do is approve atleast ONE of the wishes.
dayTwoMeeting: ^Hey how'd you enjoy your first day on the job?
^I don't know if I'm cut out for this

c-0: ^That is why I picked you after all.
c-1: ^Just pay attention to what customers are saying and listen out for any information that might help you understand their needs better.
^Also don't forget to ask questions if you need them to elaborate on anything.
^If you're still a bit unclear on our procedure just check the handbook, trust that everything you might need to know is covered in there.
^You just need to read through things carefully.

dayTwoMeetingEnd: ^Anways, today we've got THREE callers and I've raised the approval quota to TWO.
^Now that you have some GeneBucks to your name make sure you check out the Incentives Catalogue, it's right at the end of the handbook.
^If you want something just circle it and I'll know. It'll be in your office in an instant.
^I recommend you pick up a newspaper as often as you can, edited by yours truly of course!
^It's a great way to check how things are tracking down there on Earth plus you might just notice some of those callers of yours make the cut with some of those crazy wishes of theirs.
^You-- I mean those humans really are fascinating...
^Alright, time to get to work. Let's make some dreams come true!
dayThreeMeeting: ^I'll try to make these brief from now on since we've both got work to do but I'm sure by now you're atleast somewhat used to the flow of things.
^Today you've got FOUR callers to deal with, though the quota is still TWO.
^Don't forget to check out that newspaper. I work hard each morning editing a new edition just for you!
^Okay I'll let you get to it then, Keep it up!
dayFourMeeting: ^You're still here, that's fantastic I knew you had it in you!
^We're over the hump now, just gotta see it through to the end of the week and then I should be able to prove this thing is viable...
^Wait you mean you're not actually the boss?

c-0: ^Of course you do! I only choose the best.
c-1: ^Duh of course I am, the company's named after me!
^Okay I can't get into it too much but I'm sure you could already deduce that this kind of operation isn't exactly industry-standard for this kind of work.
^In fact it's not even something we would normally consider 'work'

dayFourMeetingEnding: ^Let's get to business shall we. You've still got FOUR callers today but i've bumped the quota up to THREE. KPI's are a little lower than I hoped this late in the week...
^But don't worry, you've got this! Over and out.
dayFiveMeeting: ^It seems you've left quite a mark here in the office and on the good folks back on earth, today the phone lines are full!
^That's right, for your final shift of our trial run here at GeneCorp you're going to be dealing with FIVE callers with a quota of THREE.
^Remember, today's your last chance to grab anything from the Catalogue so you might as well spend up whatever you've got left.
